description: §18.9 — a bare `match ...` written DIRECTLY in markup content (a <div> body, not inside a `${...}` logic interpolation) is kept as text by the block-splitter and SHALL fire E-TYPE-026. (S441: moved from the <program> body, which is code now, into a <div>.)
rationale: §18.9: `match` is not valid directly in markup; wrap it in a logic interpolation (`${ match subject { ... } }`) so the parser recognises it as a statement rather than text content. A bare markup-level `match` fires E-TYPE-026. ⛑ S441: a `<program>` body is no longer markup content (§40.8 S441 bullet — a bare run there is code), so the case now places the match in a <div> body, the markup locus E-TYPE-026 names.
